evidence.finding: Before the incident, actual volume averaged one call below forecast; from 09:15 onward, every interval exceeded forecast by 19–57 calls.
Post-incident offered volume increased across all queues by 48.9%–65.8%, showing a broad demand increase rather than localized misrouting.
Scheduled and logged-in staffing remained at 49 agents; productive staffing averaged 45.64 after onset versus 45.2 before onset.
Occupancy rose from a 68.1% pre-incident average to 98.9% after onset, while abandonment and delay increased materially.
Service level fell from 94.4% at 09:00 to 51.3% at 09:15 and remained below the 80% target thereafter.
No platform, routing, or other operational event was recorded during the visible window.

primary_root_cause_detail: A sustained, center-wide demand spike began at 09:15. Offered calls exceeded forecast by 24.4%–72.2% in every subsequent interval, overwhelming otherwise stable staffing capacity.
recommended_actions: Activate intraday surge staffing or cross-skilled overflow when actual volume materially exceeds forecast.
Add real-time volume-versus-forecast alerts with escalation thresholds before occupancy reaches saturation.
Review the source of the 09:15 demand increase and incorporate any recurring driver into future forecasts and contingency plans.

rejected_hypotheses.reason: Headcount did not fall: scheduled and logged-in staffing stayed at 49, while productive staffing was stable or slightly higher after onset.
Post-onset AHT averaged approximately 0.24% below forecast, and queue-level changes were negligible.
Demand and service degradation occurred across every queue, with unchanged queue staffing rather than a localized capacity shift.
No platform event was recorded, and the observed pattern is explained by excess demand against stable capacity.
Reported service level matched the prescribed formula in all 16 intervals, with zero recalculation difference.

stakeholder_summary: The service-level incident was most likely caused by an unexpected, sustained demand spike beginning at 09:15. Staffing and AHT remained stable, no platform or routing event was identified, and the reported service-level decline was mathematically valid.
